title: Musa was given the Book too. This is not new.
subtitle: The same guidance sent before
then: The Makkans called the message strange. Allah reminds them that Musa was given the Book as {idea}guidance for the Children of Israel{/idea}. Qatadah said the line about meeting him refers to {reward}the Night of Isra{/reward}, when the Prophet ﷺ met Musa.
now: Someone at work says your faith is outdated, a set of new rules. {idea}It is the oldest message there is.{/idea} Musa carried it, and the Prophets before and after him. You are in a long line.
old: My faith is something I picked up from my family.
new: I belong to a message carried by Musa and every Prophet.
try: Read the story of Musa in one short passage of the Qur'an this week.

title: Leaders who guide come from patience and certainty.
subtitle: What makes someone worth following
then: Ibn Kathir says leaders arose among them {idea}because they were patient{/idea} in following Allah's commands and believed firmly. When they later twisted the Book, {trap}they lost that position{/trap}. Sufyan said a man cannot be an example unless he shuns the temptation of this world.
now: You are the eldest sibling, the team lead, the parent everyone watches. {idea}People follow what you hold back from{/idea}, not just what you say. Patience is what turns you into someone worth copying.
old: To lead people, I need to be impressive.
new: To lead people well, I need patience and firm faith.
try: Resist one small temptation today, knowing someone younger is watching you.

title: Your Lord will settle every disagreement on that Day.
subtitle: The final judge of what people differed over
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning {idea}what they differed over, in beliefs and actions{/idea}. The disagreements of this life will have a final answer.
now: The comment thread that never ends. The family dispute about an inheritance, five years old now. {idea}Not every argument needs settling by you.{/idea} Some you can leave with the Judge who knows everything.
old: If I do not win this argument, the truth loses.
new: Allah will settle what we differ over. I can speak once and let go.
try: Step out of one online or family argument today without having the last word.

title: They walk through the homes of nations that vanished.
subtitle: Lessons in the ruins

row.title: empty dwellings
sub: as if no one lived there

then: Ibn Kathir says the deniers walked where earlier nations had lived, {trap}yet no trace of them was left{/trap}. In what happened to them, and how the believers were saved, are {idea}signs and important lessons{/idea}.
now: A holiday among ancient ruins. You take selfies by columns where a whole city once lived and planned. {idea}They thought they would last too.{/idea} The question the verse asks is: will you not listen?
old: Old ruins are just tourist spots.
new: Every ruin asks me what I am building that will last.
try: Next time you pass an old building or grave, stop and reflect for one minute.

title: Water driven to dead land, and crops spring up.
subtitle: A sign of kindness and of resurrection
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah explains {reward}His kindness and goodness{/reward} by sending water, from the sky or rivers from the mountains, to land that needs it. He titles it: {idea}the revival of the earth is proof of the resurrection{/idea}.
now: The bread in your lunch, the rice on the table, the milk in your tea. {reward}All of it started as water on dry ground.{/reward} Look at your plate before eating and you are looking at a sign.
new: Every meal began with water Allah drove to dead land.
try: Before your next meal, look at the food for a moment and say bismillah slowly.

title: When is this judgement, if you are telling the truth?
subtitle: Mocking the promised Day
then: Ibn Kathir says the disbelievers taunted: all we see of you and your companions is that {trap}you are hiding, afraid and humiliated{/trap}. They asked to hasten it because they thought {trap}it would never happen{/trap}.
now: Someone laughs at your fasting, your prayer, your patience. Where is all this getting you? {idea}The answer has not arrived yet, and that is not the same as never.{/idea} Keep going.
old: If the reward is not visible now, maybe it is not real.
new: Not yet is not never. What Allah promised is on its way.
try: When someone mocks your practice, answer kindly in one line, then carry on.

title: On that Day, late belief will not help.
subtitle: The Day of Judgement leaves no extra time
then: Ibn Kathir says some thought Al-Fath meant the conquest of Makkah. But {idea}on that day the Prophet ﷺ accepted the Islam{/idea} of nearly two thousand people. So it means {trap}Allah's Judgement{/trap}, when belief no longer helps.
now: You keep a list for later: start praying properly, pay back the debt, make up with your sister. {trap}There is a day when later runs out.{/trap} Every item on that list is still possible today.
old: I will believe properly and change once I am sure.
new: Belief only helps while there is still time to live it.
try: Take one item from your later list and do it today.

title: Turn away from them and wait. They are waiting too.
subtitle: Patience while the outcome unfolds
then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ was told to {idea}turn from them and convey what was revealed{/idea}, and wait for Allah's promise, for He never breaks it. They waited too, plotting. He ends the surah: {reward}sufficient for us is Allah{/reward}.
now: The colleague who keeps waiting for you to slip. The relative who says your new habits will not last. {idea}You do not have to fight every comment.{/idea} Keep doing the right thing and wait for Allah.
old: I need to prove myself to everyone who doubts me.
new: I can keep doing right and leave the outcome to Allah.
try: Say hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil the next time someone's doubt gets to you.
